newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA INVITES IMF MISSION ON MAY 6.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA INVITES IMF MISSION ON MAY 6.

text.p: The leader of Bulgaria's reformist Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) and likely next prime minister, Ivan Kostov, has invited an IMF mission next month to complete reform preparations agreed in March.
Kostov is expected to be nominated prime minister on Thursday after the UDF won an outright parliamentary majority in Saturday's election.

"We invited an International Monetary Fund policy mission to start work from May 6...there is a lot of work to be done," Kostov told state radio after meeting with the IMF resident representative in Sofia Franek Rozwadowski.
The IMF Sofia office said they will convey the message to the Fund's headquarters in Washington.
"We need to finalise the draft amendments to the Banks and Lending Act, the Bulgarian National Bank Act, the Trade Act, and to revise the budget frame for this year's budget," said Kostov.

Under a $548 million 20-month standby agreement sealed with the Fund earlier this month, Bulgaria pledged to introduce in June a self-regulating restrictive monetary mechanism, known as a currency board, aimed to restore confidence in the shaky financial system.

Under the currency board system the lev will be pegged to an anchor currency, the dollar or the German mark, at a rate that cannot be adjusted. The amount of levs in circulation must be matched precisely by the amount of foreign exchange reserves.

The cabinet, due to take office next month, is expected to set the exchange rate and the anchor currency jointly with the IMF and pass it to parliament for approval along with the other legal amendments needed to make the board operational, said an IMF official who declined to be named.
The lev will be pegged at a rate slightly lower than the current 1,496 to the dollar, said recently caretaker prime minister Stefan Sofianski.
Bulgaria's macroeconomic performance has improved in the past month and the 1997 budget frame agreed with the interim cabinet in March will need to be adjusted to the new indicators, said Kostov.

First signs of stabilisation were seen after the two-month rule of the caretaker cabinet, which brought down monthly inflation to 12 percent in March from 243 percent in February and stopped the free fall of the lev from an all-time low of 3,000 per dollar in February. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
